editions.title: Amazon's AI spend, Microsoft buyouts and a neocloud wobble
editions.notification: Amazon's AWS grew 39% but free cash flow turned deeply negative. Here is why AI spending is squeezing Big Tech.
editions.intro:
Amazon dominated the period. Its third-quarter results showed Amazon Web Services growing 39% to $46bn, with a backlog of $578bn, but revenue and earnings per share came in slightly below forecasts and shares fell as much as 7% in extended trading. Free cash flow over the past year slipped to minus $42.4bn, largely from AI capital spending. Chief executive Andy Jassy said AWS should grow more than 40% in 2027 and 2028 and that Amazon will spend meaningfully more on AI next year.

The cash squeeze is a wider theme. A Reuters analysis of LSEG data finds that Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle returned the smallest share of their cash to shareholders in at least 15 years, with buybacks down 83%. Their combined capital spending of $556.9bn exceeded operating cash flow, leaving a free cash flow deficit of $14bn. Meanwhile Microsoft is offering voluntary severance to about 60,000 staff while protecting AI-critical teams, and its AI infrastructure budget is about $170bn for 2026.

Doubts about the AI build-out are growing. Shares in neocloud firms such as CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have fallen by about a quarter in a month, and Nvidia quietly lowered published bandwidth targets for its Vera Rubin hardware. Reports also say OpenAI has cut its fundraising target by $10bn. Against that backdrop, Oracle shares rose about 14% during its AI World conference, though they remain well below their late 2025 high.

top_stories.title: AWS grows 39% but Amazon's cash burn deepens
top_stories.summary: Amazon posted record operating margins and a 39% jump in AWS revenue, but results were slightly below forecasts and shares fell sharply after hours. Free cash flow of minus $42.4bn shows how heavily AI spending is weighing on the business, and Jassy signalled more investment in 2027.

top_stories.title: Big Tech buybacks fall 83% as AI spending outruns cash
top_stories.summary: Five hyperscalers returned the smallest share of cash to shareholders in at least 15 years. Their capex exceeded operating cash flow, with the gap funded by reserves, borrowing and share sales, despite more than $3tn in AI commitments.

top_stories.summary: Microsoft is offering buyouts to about 60,000 employees, excluding data centres, sales, cybersecurity and quantum teams. It is the second such programme this year and comes as it keeps AI infrastructure spending near $170bn.

top_stories.title: Neocloud shares slump as bubble fears grow
top_stories.summary: CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN and Applied Digital have lost about a quarter of their value in a month, weighed by heavy debt and rising borrowing costs. A Microsoft deal cancellation and lower spending forecasts have added to the unease.

top_stories.title: Nvidia quietly trims Vera Rubin bandwidth specs
top_stories.summary: Nvidia reduced published memory and interconnect bandwidth for Vera Rubin hardware without a press release. Analysts read it as a fallback after memory suppliers struggled to hit target speeds, which could help AMD's rival parts look better on paper.

top_stories.title: OpenAI reportedly cuts fundraising target by $10bn
top_stories.summary: According to the Financial Times, OpenAI is now seeking about $20bn at a valuation near $1.25tn, a reduction that is framed as tempering ambitions amid sector anxiety. Details are limited in the available summary.

editions.title: DoorDash buys Instacart; tech sell-off deepens over AI spending
editions.notification: DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart for about $17bn as AI spending worries rattle tech stocks.
editions.intro:
The biggest development is DoorDash's agreed deal to buy rival Instacart at $65 a share, a 26% premium, valuing the business at roughly $17 billion. The cash-heavy offer still needs regulatory and shareholder approval, and it would leave iPhone users with one fewer app-based grocery and delivery option. The deal lands amid a sharp slide in US tech shares, with the Nasdaq posting its worst month since March 2025.

That selloff is driven by fears about the roughly $800 billion that Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon and Microsoft are committing to spending in 2026. Intel fell 28% after warning of weaker PC demand, while Reddit dropped 29% after weak user numbers and complaints that Google's AI search is cutting its referral traffic. Reddit's CEO said Google's AI Mode does not drive meaningful traffic, and Alphabet's core ad growth slowed to its weakest pace in five quarters even as it kept capex guidance of up to $205 billion.

The AI nervousness also shows up in private markets. The Financial Times reports that OpenAI has cut its fundraising target by $10 billion, citing the AI selloff and Anthropic's forthcoming listing; Anthropic's IPO filing, meanwhile, shows $16.3 billion of first-half revenue alongside heavy losses. Apple, by contrast, retook the title of the world's most valuable listed company, supported by iPhone demand and its China AI rollout.

editions.title: Alphabet sheds $500bn as AI spending doubts hit Big Tech and Intel crashes
editions.notification: Alphabet loses $500bn in a day as AI spending doubts spread; Intel slumps on weak PC outlook.
editions.intro:
Investor patience with AI spending cracked this week. Alphabet lost just over $500bn in value after its quarterly update showed AI summaries in search weighing on advertising, with free cash flow negative by over $9bn. Amazon's free cash flow also swung deeply negative and its shares fell in after-hours trading, while Microsoft's shares barely moved despite 19% revenue growth. A global tech sell-off was reported to be deepening as the Nikkei and Wall Street opened lower.

Intel was the sharpest casualty. Its shares fell by roughly a quarter after third-quarter client chip revenue dropped and the company guided fourth-quarter revenue and earnings below expectations, blaming a memory shortage that is squeezing PC demand. Intel expects the PC market to shrink 12% this year. Reddit, meanwhile, said search referrals had fallen sharply and it will move to a logged-in-only experience, a direct example of how AI search is reshaping traffic.

Crypto was hit by a major security failure. Binance said an attacker drained hot wallets, with the affected amount put at about $6.3bn, and it pledged to cover losses from its SAFU fund and company money. Separately, reports that Nvidia's chief executive had ties to a Singapore businesswoman suspected by US intelligence of helping Beijing are unverified and have been strongly denied by Nvidia. Dealmaking continued, with DoorDash agreeing to buy Instacart for about $17bn and the FCC approving Amazon's Globalstar acquisition.

top_stories.title: Alphabet loses $500bn as AI search fears hit shares
top_stories.summary: Alphabet fell almost 13% to a six-month low after AI summaries in search were blamed for weaker ad revenue, even though Google Cloud grew 103%. Amazon also fell after-hours on negative free cash flow, while Microsoft held up better. The reaction shows investors increasingly questioning the payoff from heavy AI spending.

top_stories.title: Intel shares plunge after weak PC chip outlook
top_stories.summary: Intel shares fell almost a quarter after client revenue fell and fourth-quarter guidance missed estimates by a wide margin. Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan blamed memory shortages and supply constraints, and forecast the PC market shrinking 12% this year. The stock had more than doubled earlier this year, so the drop is steep.

top_stories.title: Binance hit by about $6.3bn crypto theft
top_stories.summary: Attackers drained Binance hot wallets, with the affected funds put at around $6.3bn, and Tether and Circle froze stablecoins to help. Binance says the likely entry point was a compromised engineer's laptop and has pledged to cover all customer losses. The SAFU reserve covers only a fraction of the amount, so company funds will carry much of the cost.

top_stories.title: Reddit moves to logged-in-only experience
top_stories.summary: Reddit will test a logged-in-only experience in select non-US markets from Q4, citing a drop of over a million search referrals a week. The CEO warned daily active users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 if the trend continues. Reddit still reported Q3 revenue up 53% to $895m.

top_stories.summary: DoorDash has agreed to acquire rival Instacart at $65 per share, a 26% premium, with at least 75% in cash. The deal still needs regulatory and shareholder approval. It would consolidate two major US grocery and delivery players.

Nothing is signed and terms could change. It would make Nvidia chip supplier, equity investor and debt backer in one chain.

editions.title: Alphabet's $500bn slide and Intel's crash rattle tech
editions.notification: Alphabet loses $500bn as AI spending doubts spread; Intel and Binance also reel
editions.intro:
Wall Street's tech earnings season turned sharply on Thursday as investors questioned how much AI spending will pay off. Alphabet shed just over $500bn in value, falling almost 13% to a six-month low, after its quarterly update showed AI summaries in search weighing on advertising revenue. Profits fell 25% and free cash flow was negative by more than $9bn, even though Google Cloud grew 103%. Amazon and Microsoft also reported strong top lines, but Amazon's free cash flow was deeply negative and its shares fell about 6% after hours, and a global tech sell-off was reported to be deepening.

Intel was the other major casualty. Its shares fell by almost a quarter after a steep drop in PC chip sales and a weak fourth-quarter forecast, with the chief executive blaming a memory-chip shortage and warning the PC market could shrink 12% this year. Datacentre and AI revenue rose 78%, but the company said it will likely not fully meet datacentre demand in the first half. Memory costs are a common thread, also hitting PC makers and smartphone shipments, which fell 20% in the third quarter.

Crypto and security stories dominated the rest of the day. Binance said an attacker drained hot wallets, with the affected funds now put at about $6.3bn; Tether and Circle froze stablecoin balances, and Binance has pledged to cover losses. Separately, a New York Times report alleging that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had ties to a Singapore businesswoman suspected of helping Beijing was met with Nvidia's denial. Several linked Nvidia items, including reported credit guarantees for Nscale, remain unconfirmed rumours.

editions.title: Binance hack, Alphabet rout and Intel slump rattle tech
editions.notification: Binance hit by a roughly $6.3bn crypto theft as Alphabet and Intel shares tumble on AI doubts.
editions.intro:
Markets and security were the dominant stories over the last 24 hours. Binance said an attacker drained its hot wallets, with the affected funds later put at about $6.3 billion. Tether and Circle froze significant stablecoin balances to help, and Binance has pledged to cover all losses from its SAFU fund and company money. The exchange blamed a likely entry point via a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, and withdrawals remain paused while it overhauls security. A crypto industry figure has said the bitcoin is probably unrecoverable, though that is an opinion rather than an official update.

Earnings reshaped the market mood. Alphabet lost just over $500bn in value after AI summaries in search weighed on ad revenue, even as Google Cloud grew 103%. Amazon's free cash flow turned sharply negative and its shares fell in after-hours trading. Intel dropped almost a quarter of its value after PC chip sales fell, with its CEO warning the PC chip market could shrink 12% next year. Taken together, investors are increasingly questioning how much AI spending will pay back.

Nvidia was the subject of several reports. The Information says it is in talks to guarantee billions of dollars of debt for Nscale's West Virginia data centre, which Anthropic plans to use under a deal worth about $45 billion. Separately, a New York Times report alleges US intelligence suspected a Singapore executive of acting for Beijing and linked her to Jensen Huang; Nvidia and the Chinese embassy have denied wrongdoing, and the claims rest on unnamed sources.

Tether and Circle froze large stablecoin balances, and Binance has pledged to cover all losses while withdrawals stay paused for a security overhaul. The SAFU fund covers only about a sixth of the amount.

editions.title: Apple's touchscreen Mac, Samsung's record profit and AI chip deals
editions.notification: Apple finally adds touchscreen MacBook Pros, and Samsung posts a record $80.5bn quarter.
editions.intro:
Apple has broken its long refusal to put touchscreens on Macs. The new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models use OLED XDR displays with touch input, and they start at $2,899 and $3,399 respectively. Pre-orders are open and shipping begins on 6 November. The launch is the first big product news under new chief executive John Ternus, and it comes with a premium price that buyers will notice.

The chip and memory sector dominated the day. Samsung reported a record third-quarter operating profit of KRW 107.4 trillion (about $80.5bn), driven by memory chips for AI data centres. Its executives said memory shortages will worsen in 2027 and persist into 2028, with long-term agreements covering 60 to 70% of capacity. Shares nonetheless slid, because profits narrowly missed some estimates and little was said about shareholder returns. Oracle, meanwhile, outlined a multi-vendor AI infrastructure push, deploying Nvidia Vera Rubin systems, AMD MI455X GPUs and Google TPUs from 2027.

On the deal front, the FCC approved Amazon's $11.5bn purchase of Globalstar, which strengthens Amazon's direct-to-device satellite ambitions and puts pressure on AST SpaceMobile. Separately, reports say OpenAI is considering buying Google TPUs, and Anthropic is weighing a retail tranche of up to 20% in its IPO. Both remain unconfirmed.

top_stories.title: Apple launches touchscreen MacBook Pro starting at $2,899
top_stories.summary: Apple has launched 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros with OLED touch displays, its first touchscreen Macs. Pre-orders are open and shipping starts 6 November. The premium pricing is $400 above the current equivalent model.

top_stories.title: Samsung posts record $80.5bn quarterly operating profit
top_stories.summary: Samsung's chip division drove a record KRW 107.4 trillion operating profit on AI memory demand. The smartphone unit posted a loss due to higher memory costs, and capex is set at KRW 84.4 trillion this year.

top_stories.title: Samsung warns memory shortages will last into 2028
top_stories.summary: Samsung says HBM4 supply for 2027 is sold out and tight memory supply will persist into 2028. Long-term agreements with 10 major customers cover 60 to 70% of its capacity.

top_stories.title: Samsung shares fall on thin investor-return detail
top_stories.summary: Samsung shares slid after quarterly profits fell just short of estimates. Investors got a bullish outlook but little detail on shareholder payouts.

top_stories.title: Oracle lines up Nvidia, AMD, Intel and Google chips
top_stories.summary: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure outlined a multi-vendor AI build-out, including Nvidia Vera Rubin, AMD MI455X and Intel Diamond Rapids. It will also be the first hyperscaler outside Google to deploy Google TPUs, from 2027.

top_stories.title: FCC clears Amazon's $11.5bn Globalstar acquisition
top_stories.summary: The FCC approved the deal, including transfer of key mobile-satellite spectrum, to support Amazon's planned direct-to-device system. Closing is expected in 2027, and AST SpaceMobile shares slipped overnight.

top_stories.title: Anthropic may reserve up to 20% of IPO for retail
top_stories.summary: Bloomberg reports Anthropic is considering a 15% to 20% retail allocation, with JPMorgan leading. The S-1 also shows heavy compute commitments and an 85% gross margin, and Senator Warren has raised questions.

Distillation claims against DeepSeek and Moonshot are unconfirmed and come from a single outlet, though Anthropic made similar accusations earlier.

in_brief.line: Alphabet's Q3 revenue rose 25% to $127.6bn, but search growth of 12% fell short and analysts expect further slowing.
Google's Gemini 4 Carbon claims top security benchmarks, priced at $2/$10 per million tokens during an introductory period.
Enphase, Opendoor and Boeing hit 52-week lows after weak results or cuts, with Enphase down about 16%.
Personal details of over 41,000 DHS staff were leaked online, with DHS investigating a potential breach.
Australia's House passed the digital duty of care bill, which would ban chatbot content simulating emotional intimacy for minors.
Ofcom set out four high-assurance age verification methods ahead of the UK under-16 social media ban due in March.
Upwind raised $400m at a $3.8bn valuation after rejecting a Datadog acquisition offer that did not include a premium.
ULA's Vulcan rocket returns to flight on 13 November, carrying 40 Amazon Leo satellites.

Finance.title: Tech sell-off on AI spending fears hits markets
Finance.notification: Chipmakers slump as AI spending fears spread, with Intel down about 30% and Nasdaq 100 off 3.5%
Finance.summary:
A global tech sell-off on Friday wiped billions from chipmakers and pushed the Nasdaq 100 down 3.5 per cent, while the S&P 500 slipped 1.8 per cent. Investors are questioning the heavy cash spending on artificial intelligence, and Intel's roughly 30 per cent fall after a weak revenue forecast led the damage. Alphabet's record one-day fall of more than 12 per cent added to the pressure, and Apple overtook Nvidia as the world's most valuable listed company.

In London the FTSE 100 ended slightly higher at 10,729.78, with AstraZeneca rising 7 per cent on strong cancer-drug sales, though NatWest fell nearly 9 per cent. Poundland's directors filed a notice to appoint administrators, putting more than 12,000 jobs at risk. Yorkshire Water's chief executive is stepping down after a poor environmental rating.

Europe faces its own pressures. France's economy shrank 0.1 per cent in the third quarter, and Fitch moved its outlook to negative, while Eurozone inflation is expected near 4 per cent and a December ECB rate rise remains possible. In Asia, the Bank of Japan held rates but signalled further tightening, and India's markets jumped after a corporate tax cut.

highlights.text: Alphabet fell over 12% in a day, its worst ever, and Intel lost about 29% after a weak forecast. Apple retook the top market value spot from Nvidia.

highlights.text: Poundland faces administration with around 12,000 jobs at risk, while AstraZeneca rose 7% on strong oncology sales and beat expectations.

highlights.text: France's economy contracted 0.1% in Q3 and Fitch cut its outlook to negative. Italian inflation jumped to 5.4%, and a December ECB hike is still possible.

highlights.label: Asia
highlights.text: The Bank of Japan held rates but guided to further tightening. India's Sensex jumped about 2,200 points after a corporate tax cut.

Lenders are becoming more selective, a possible constraint on funding America's AI build-out.
Lula's victory in Brazil weakened the real, pushing agricultural commodity prices lower.
Tata Motors has taken control of Iveco after its tender offer, valued at about $4.32bn.

World.title: Tech sell-off, Binance hack and US midterm fights dominate
World.notification: Google's record $500bn one-day loss rattles AI-linked stocks as Binance's $6.3bn hack deepens the crypto selloff
World.summary:
Markets have had a rough run. Alphabet fell more than 12% after third-quarter results missed expectations, wiping about $500 billion from its value in the biggest one-day loss in its history. Investors are worried that AI spending may erode search, and tech shares fell for a second day as Amazon and Intel results raised concerns about heavy capital expenditure. Separately, Binance reported a $6.3bn hack, which the FBI has linked to North Korea, pushing bitcoin and other major cryptocurrencies lower.

In the US, the midterm elections on 3 November are dominating politics. The Justice Department is pressing election disputes in California and Alaska, courts have repeatedly blocked moves to set aside ballots, and the Michigan Senate race is strained by a bitter feud between Abdul El-Sayed and Haley Stevens. Oil prices rose after a tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran reporting mine strikes and Houthi claims adding to supply fears.

In the UK, Andy Burnham said he is open to a formal slavery apology but not reparations, while Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is expected to unveil settlement reforms next week. In Europe, France faces a third weekend of protests, Fitch revised its France outlook to negative, and Poland's constitutional court stand-off has drawn riot police. In Asia, the US, Japan and South Korea reaffirmed their call for North Korea's denuclearisation, and Foxconn said it is working on a tie-up with OpenAI.

Air defences were deployed at Mar-a-Lago and Palm Beach airport ahead of the midterms amid a heightened threat environment.

Tech.title: Tech shares slide as AI spending fears mount
Tech.notification: Tech stocks fall again as investors question the near $1tn AI spending spree
Tech.summary:
US tech shares fell for a second straight session as investors grew uneasy about the huge sums being poured into AI. Intel dropped 28% after flagging weaker PC demand, Alphabet slid further after its earlier plunge, and Reddit fell 29% on weak user figures and concerns that Google's AI search is squeezing referral traffic. The Nasdaq ended October with its worst month since March 2025.

Behind the sell-off is a broader worry about cash. Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle are together spending close to $1tn on AI, and a Reuters analysis shows their capital spending in the first nine months of 2026 exceeded operating cash flow, with buybacks down 83%. Amazon's results added to the picture: strong AWS growth of 39%, but a sharp drop in free cash flow and a warning of even bigger AI spending in 2027.

Doubts are spreading beyond the giants. Neocloud firms such as CoreWeave have lost about a quarter of their value in a month, OpenAI has reportedly cut its fundraising target by $10bn, and investors are trimming growth stocks. Apple's rise back to the top of the market-value table stands out against this backdrop.

highlights.label: Intel
highlights.text: Intel shares fell 28% after signalling weaker PC demand into the first half of next year and cash spending above cash generated.

highlights.label: Amazon
highlights.text: AWS grew 39% to $46bn, but free cash flow over the past year fell to minus $42.4bn and shares dropped as much as 7% after hours.

highlights.label: OpenAI
highlights.text: OpenAI is reportedly seeking about $20bn at a $1.25tn valuation, $10bn less than planned, as AI jitters grow.

highlights.label: Reddit
highlights.text: Reddit's CEO says Google's AI Mode does not drive traffic, as search referrals fell by over 1 million a week in October.

highlights.label: Microsoft
highlights.text: Microsoft is offering voluntary severance to about 60,000 staff while keeping AI-critical teams protected, and plans around $170bn of AI infrastructure spending in 2026.

highlights.label: DoorDash
highlights.text: DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart at $65 a share, about $17bn, a 26% premium, mostly in cash, subject to approval.

points.text: Reuters: Big Tech buybacks fell 83% in the first nine months of 2026 as capex of $556.9bn outran operating cash flow.
Nvidia quietly cut published bandwidth targets for Vera Rubin hardware, a move analysts read as a fallback on memory speeds.
Nvidia's store has stopped listing the RTX 5080 after the RTX 5090 disappeared, with street prices about 2.2 times launch price.

LiveWire warns it may not survive as a going concern; shares fell over 40% after it withdrew full-year guidance.

Fashion.title: Capri lifts outlook as luxury houses pivot to culture
Fashion.notification: Capri lifts its outlook and shares surge as the Louvre ends its strike threat with a union deal.
Fashion.summary:
Capri Holdings, owner of Michael Kors, Jimmy Choo and, until December 2025, Versace, dominated the day's fashion business news. It reported second-quarter revenue ahead of company and analyst expectations, said total revenue should return to growth in the second half of fiscal 2027, and kept Jimmy Choo out of any sale talk. Michael Kors Americas fell 11%, while Jimmy Choo Americas rose 24%, which shows why the group is leaning on its smaller luxury label.

Elsewhere, luxury brands are looking beyond clothing for cultural relevance. Lemaire is using an art exhibition in Paris as a response to slowing sales, and Louis Vuitton's men's pre-collection, designed by Pharrell Williams, leaned on a weather theme and technical footwear. Leadership change also featured, with Dries Van Noten appointing Adrian Ward-Rees as president.

The Louvre reached a deal with unions after months of strike threats, offering 50 new security hires in 2027 and a monthly raise, though the renovation's cost and scope remain contested. Across the wider sector, Puma's sales slowed less than expected, Trent rose on profit growth, and Nanushka is under financial strain.

highlights.text: Quarterly revenue beat expectations and Jimmy Choo is said to be able to reach $800m. Michael Kors Americas fell 11%.
